title: Jailer 2 Dips 20 Percent on Tuesday, India Gross Reaches Rs 462.75 Crore
headline: Jailer 2 Dips 20 Percent on Tuesday, India Gross Reaches Rs 462.75 Crore
subheadline: Pinkvilla puts the second-Tuesday gross at Rs 8.75 crore and the India total at Rs 462.75 crore, while Sacnilk's nett count stands at Rs 415.65 crore with worldwide gross near Rs 744 crore.
summary: Pinkvilla puts the second-Tuesday gross at Rs 8.75 crore and the India total at Rs 462.75 crore, while Sacnilk's nett count stands at Rs 415.65 crore with worldwide gross near Rs 744 crore.
excerpt: Pinkvilla puts the second-Tuesday gross at Rs 8.75 crore and the India total at Rs 462.75 crore, while Sacnilk's nett count stands at Rs 415.65 crore with worldwide gross near Rs 744 crore.
body:
• Jailer 2 collected Rs 8.75 crore gross in India on its second Tuesday, a 20 per cent drop from Monday, taking its India gross to Rs 462.75 crore, according to Pinkvilla.
  • On Sacnilk's nett measure, the film earned Rs 7.50 crore on Tuesday, down 20.6 per cent, for an India nett total of Rs 415.65 crore and a worldwide gross estimated at about Rs 744 crore.
  • Pinkvilla expects the Rajinikanth starrer to close its second week near Rs 480 crore gross in India and to cross Rs 500 crore domestically if the current trend holds.
  • In Tamil Nadu, the film is expected to enter the Rs 200 crore club in its third weekend; it is already the record Tamil grosser in Karnataka and Kerala.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 eased on its second Tuesday, collecting Rs 8.75 crore gross at the Indian box office, down 20 per cent from the previous day, according to Pinkvilla. The day's business took the film's running India gross to Rs 462.75 crore in 13 days, keeping the Nelson Dilipkumar directorial on course for a second-week close of around Rs 480 crore.

The two main trackers put the same Tuesday on different measures, and the distinction matters. Pinkvilla reports gross collections. Sacnilk, whose estimates were reported by The Indian Witness, reports nett: Rs 7.50 crore on Tuesday, a fall of 20.6 per cent from Monday's Rs 9.45 crore nett, across 10,664 shows. On that measure the film's India nett total stands at Rs 415.65 crore, its India gross at Rs 486.50 crore and its worldwide gross at about Rs 744 crore, including roughly Rs 257.50 crore from overseas. Tracker estimates differ in method, so the gross totals are not directly interchangeable.

"In Tamil Nadu, the film is expected to enter the Rs 200 crore club in its third weekend; it is already the record Tamil grosser in Karnataka and Kerala."

A second week that is holding, not fading

The pattern of the second week explains why trade watchers describe this as a hold rather than a slide. After an eight-day first week of Rs 374 crore gross on Pinkvilla's table, the film collected Rs 16 crore on its second Friday, jumped to Rs 26 crore on Saturday and Rs 27.25 crore on Sunday, then settled to Rs 10.75 crore on Monday and Rs 8.75 crore on Tuesday, Box Office Worldwide reported. Weekday drops of this size are standard after a strong weekend; the test is the level the film settles at, and a Tuesday above Rs 8 crore gross in week two is a high floor.

Sacnilk's occupancy data points the same way. Overall occupancy on Tuesday was about 18.3 per cent, with an estimated 6.09 lakh tickets sold. The Tamil version recorded 21.2 per cent occupancy and the Kannada version about 22 per cent, ahead of Telugu at 20.2 per cent and Hindi at 14 per cent.

Records beyond Tamil Nadu

The sequel, backed by Sun Pictures and starring Rajinikanth as retired jailer Tiger Muthuvel Pandian alongside Shiva Rajkumar, Mohanlal, Jackie Shroff and S. J. Suryah, with music by Anirudh Ravichander, has already become the record Tamil grosser in Karnataka and Kerala, according to Pinkvilla. Its Hindi dubbed version is marching towards a Rs 40 crore final, a strong total for a Tamil-dubbed film that has not released in the national chains.

The worldwide picture has moved since our earlier reporting. The film became the highest-grossing Tamil film ever at Rs 710 crore worldwide earlier this week, after reaching Rs 443 crore in India after its second weekend. Sacnilk's latest worldwide estimate of about Rs 744 crore puts the Rs 750 crore mark within reach in the coming days.

What to watch next

Two milestones now frame the rest of the run. In India, the film needs roughly Rs 37 crore more in gross collections to cross Rs 500 crore, a mark Pinkvilla says current trends point to. In Tamil Nadu, it is expected to enter the Rs 200 crore club during its third weekend. How far the weekday numbers settle this week will decide whether those marks fall this weekend or the next.

For diaspora audiences in North America and the Gulf, the overseas contribution of about Rs 257.50 crore on Sacnilk's estimate underlines how much of this run is being powered outside India as well. The film remains in theatres in its Tamil original and dubbed versions.
